title: Nothing teaches the game — three end-state options
for: Bailey. Pick one, or name the parts you want from each.
approvedIdea: Cold open and taught chapter (Bailey, 2026-09-19). The other four onboarding proposals were NOT approved and appear nowhere here: no medals, no challenge ribbons, no accessibility pack, no HUD density presets.
drivenBy: critic/rounds/round-03.md issue 1 — onboarding 2.8 / 10, the number one issue on the live build
docs/plans/onboarding-review.md — paper critique, verdict 'revise', 14 required changes
AGENTS.md hard rule 9 (end state first) and hard rule 14 (every change is game-aware)
resolution: 1600x900, HTML composited with docs/concepts/polish/_kit over real captures from the live build (main 7191674). Rendered with PYREFLY_BROWSER=gpu.
constraintsCommonToAllThree: Every option has a visible skip and a visible 'never show again' on the first surface it puts on screen. No option can be entered without seeing both.
One teaching surface at a time: while a coaching surface is up, the move advisor card and any mid-battle bark are suppressed (paper critique REQUIRED 4).
Player words only, never developer words: 'turn order', 'the gauge', 'Overdrive', 'aeon', 'dressphere', 'chain'. The acronyms CTB and ATB appear nowhere on any frame (REQUIRED 14).
Keyed by MECHANIC, not by chapter — the first time turn order, an Overdrive, a gauge or a chain is real. None of these boards depends on the unbuilt Macalania or Leblanc chapters (REQUIRED 1).
An existing save with a cleared chapter is a veteran: every id pre-marked seen, coaching off (REQUIRED 7). A veteran sees none of this.
Suppression ships with the feature: ?coach=off plus __pyrefly.setCoaching(false), so Playwright, the screenshot tool and the critic's Part C composites never see it (REQUIRED 8).

options.title: Taught first turn
options.pitch: A short cold open states the one thing a newcomer cannot guess — these are two games with two different clocks — and then three coach marks land on the real HUD, one at a time, at the moment each thing first matters.

frames.moment: the very first screen after the title
notes: Title painting stays on screen; a paper slab slides in over it, so nothing new has to be painted.
Two cards, side by side, say the only thing a newcomer cannot work out: I-III are turn-based, IV-V are real time.
A START HERE ribbon names Chapter I and one line says why, so a friend who jumps to Chapter V is a choice, not an accident.
Three keys on the footer: Enter begin, Esc skip straight to the chapters, D never show this again.
Budget: readable and skipped inside 3 s; the measured 60 s to first deliberate action is counted from the chapter card, not from here.

frames.moment: the first player turn, FFX — mark 1 of 3
notes: The whole frame dims to 70 percent ink except the turn-order column, which keeps its full paint and takes a gold border.
The mark names what is lit in three sentences and stops: turn order, slow versus fast, and that nothing moves until you choose.
The turn is held until one confirm press — true to FFX, whose engine holds the turn anyway (research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md row 3).
The advisor card and the next-best-move bark are suppressed for this beat; the intent panel is behind the dim, not stacked beside the mark.
Three marks total across the chapter — turn order, Overdrive ready, and what a loss meant — then never again.

frames.moment: FFX-2, and where help is reached afterwards
notes: No dim and no hold: a pink 'GAUGES STILL RUNNING' tag sits above the mark and the fight does not stop, because X-2 never stops to teach.
The mark names the gauge and the second colour that runs down before a move lands — the charge phase the real game already draws.
A small ink card offers Wait mode once, at the chapter's start, in X-2's own voice; whatever is picked is respected from then on.
Help afterwards lives where canon puts it: Pause, Options, Battle Help — a real FFX-2 Config entry, so the label is not invented.
Same three-mark budget, same skip and never-again keys, different chrome: pink spine, mirrored, anchored to the other edge.

options.whatItTeaches: Turn order (FFX) and the gauge (FFX-2) on the first turn; Overdrive when the bar first fills; why you lost on the defeat screen. Three marks per game, then silence forever.
options.risk: It is the only option that puts something between the title and the game. If the cold open is a beat too long it is the first thing a returning player resents, and Part C reads a slab over the approved title painting as 'something added'.

gameAware.ffxOnly: The mark holds the turn until a confirm press, and mark 1 points at the turn-order list. Source: research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §9 row 3 — the turn-order preview is TRUE for FFX and NOT TRUE for FFX-2; FFX's CTB waits for input by definition.
gameAware.ffx2Only: Nothing is ever frozen: the mark is non-blocking, rendered beside the party rows while all three gauges fill. Mark 1 points at the gauge and names its charge phase. The Active/Wait choice is offered once. Sources: research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §4.2 / FC-4 (four-phase gauge: green fill, command input, purple charge, execution and recovery) and §4.3 / FC-5 (the charge segment is canon's own answer to 'what does this cost'), plus the Wait/Active indicator the game toggles by itself.
gameAware.both: The cold open, the START HERE ribbon, the seen-set, the off switch and the suppression hooks — shared plumbing, CHK-020. Both games also ship canon precedent for 'full the first time, short after': FFX's Config Aeons Short, FFX-2's Spherechanges toggle with its always-full-first-time override.

options.title: Field notes
options.pitch: Nothing is ever interrupted. The title goes straight to the chapter board, a single line appears on the hint bar the first time a system shows up, and a two-page HOW TO PLAY is there whenever anyone wants it.

frames.moment: the very first screen after the title — which is the board itself
notes: This option adds no screen at all. The title still goes where it goes today.
Two things are new on the board: a START HERE ribbon with one line of why, and an H — HOW TO PLAY entry beside the existing hint row.
Every chapter card carries one line saying which game it is and how that game moves, on the card, so it never has to be dismissed.
Nothing here can be skipped because nothing here interrupts; the never-show-again is instead a 'hide notes' key inside the fight.
Cheapest of the three and the only one that adds no time at all in front of a returning player.

frames.moment: the first player turn, FFX — taught without stopping
notes: No dim, no hold, no confirm. One line arrives on the bottom hint bar and leaves on its own.
The teaching is really done by the HUD: the turn-order list shows a dashed ghost slot where this move would put you, before you commit.
That preview is the approved 'the queue answers before you commit' item, already half-built in the code (previewRank) and simply made legible.
The bar carries its own two keys at the right: H for the full page, D to stop showing notes.
Weakest on a player who is not looking at the bottom of the screen — which is the honest risk of a surface nobody is forced to read.

frames.moment: how help is reached again, from the title menu or the pause menu, any time
notes: HOW TO PLAY is a row on the existing pause menu and a page in the approved pause chrome — no new page style is invented (paper critique OPTIONAL 15).
Page 1 is the two games side by side: turn order, Overdrive and aeon on the left; the gauge, dressphere and chain on the right.
Each term gets one still from the real game, so a word is never explained only in words.
Page 2 holds the controls, the vocabulary, and the line that says why you lost and what to try — the half of the rubric row nothing covers today.
Reachable mid-fight without losing the fight, which is the case where a newcomer actually goes looking.

options.whatItTeaches: Turn order, the gauge, Overdrive, aeon, dressphere and chain — each named once on the hint bar when it first appears, and all of them permanently in the codex.
options.risk: It can be missed entirely. A player who reads nothing learns nothing, and 'nothing teaches the game' could survive this option if the hint lines are not worded very well.

gameAware.ffxOnly: The dashed ghost slot and the 'you act again here' preview on the turn-order list. Source: research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §9 row 3 and §4.1 — the Act List preview is FFX only, including the rank-3 assumption for every other unit. FFX-2 must never be given a queue.
gameAware.ffx2Only: The FFX-2 hint bar names the gauge and its charge segment instead, and the codex's right column carries dressphere and chain. Sources: §4.2 / FC-4 and §4.3 / FC-5; the chain counter is listed as FFX-2 only in §9.
gameAware.both: The hint bar itself, the codex page, the START HERE ribbon, the 'why you lost' line and the hide-notes key — shared plumbing, CHK-020, same work in both games with different content.

options.title: Auron's briefing
options.pitch: Twenty seconds in the game's own voice, before anything else, framing both clocks as a character would say them. After that the game says almost nothing — one whispered line, the first time something is genuinely real.

frames.moment: the very first screen after the title — the briefing
notes: Auron's approved painting over an approved backdrop; four lines of speech, a thin timer, and the skip line.
He says the only two rules that matter and says them as opinions: in mine nothing moves until you move, in hers the clock does not wait.
Skippable from the very first frame with Esc; D retires it for good; it never plays twice on its own.
Twenty seconds, timed, with the progress visible — a player can see how long they are agreeing to.
The same still and the same sentence become the link preview card and the favicon frame, which the site does not have today.

frames.moment: the first player turn, FFX — one line, first use only
notes: No numbered course, no dim, no panel of rules — the briefing already said it, so this is a reminder, not a lesson.
One line in Auron's register, in the serif, over empty sky: he moves after you, not before, use it.
The turn is held for exactly one confirm press, which is what FFX's engine does with a turn anyway.
The hint bar gains one key so the briefing can be called back, so the line never has to explain itself.
Roughly three of these exist per game and each fires exactly once, ever.

frames.moment: FFX-2 in its own voice, and how the briefing is reached again
notes: A different character and a completely different register: Rikku, mid-fight, not a narrator.
The line fades on its own — nothing is held, no key is required, and all three gauges keep filling behind it.
Two permanent pause rows appear: replay the briefing, or turn the voices off for good.
Nothing inside a fight ever asks a second time, which is what keeps this option off a veteran's back.
Open question for you: canon's own X-2 tutorial voice is Shinra on the Celsius, already cited in our shipped data. Rikku is the warmer read; Shinra is the sourced one.

options.whatItTeaches: Both clocks, once, in character, before the first chapter; then turn order, Overdrive and the gauge as single lines the first time each one is live.
options.risk: It is the most charming and the least explicit. A player who skips the briefing gets very little afterwards, and writing voice lines that teach without being cute is the hardest copy job of the three. It also needs a voice that exists in both games or two separate ones, which doubles the copy.

gameAware.ffxOnly: Auron carries the FFX half and the line holds the turn for one confirm. FFX chapters are 1 to 3. Source: research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §9 row 3 plus the paper critique's REQUIRED 6 — FFX's own in-battle teaching halts the fight, so holding the turn is true to FFX.
gameAware.ffx2Only: An FFX-2 voice, non-blocking, fading on its own with every gauge running. FFX-2 chapters are 4 and 5. Source: the paper critique's REQUIRED 6 and research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §4.2 — freezing an Active-mode X-2 fight to teach is the one thing X-2 never does. Canon's attested X-2 tutorial voice is Shinra's on the Celsius (src/data/ffx2/garment-grids/early.ts:30).
gameAware.both: The briefing slot, the timer, the skip, the never-again, the replay row and the suppression hooks — shared plumbing, CHK-020.

questionsForBailey: Which option, or which parts of which? You can take A's three marks with B's codex, or C's briefing with B's hint bar — the frames are built so they mix.

The FFX-2 Config list in our sources names a real entry called Battle Help, so that label is canon for FFX-2. The FFX Config list we have sourced names no equivalent. Do you want the same words used in FFX (ours, honest but not canon), or a different FFX label?
Option C's FFX-2 voice: Rikku (warmer, in the fight) or Shinra (canon's own tutorial voice, already cited in our shipped data)?
Do you want the taught chapter flagged START HERE on the chapter board? The paper critique says yes and no hard lock. All three options assume yes; say the word and it comes off.
notBuilt: Nothing under src/ was touched. These are mockups only; per hard rule 9 nothing is built until you pick.
openDependencies: Round-02 #26, #27 and #29 (research citations printing in the intent slab, blank info slab on leaf rows, the strategy guide clipping mid-sentence) are the cheapest teaching in the game and should land before any of this.
Round-02 #30 (Chapter 1's 38.6 s pre-scene cannot be fast-forwarded) — otherwise a cold open pushes first input past two minutes.
A 390x844 variant of the picked option still has to be drawn; the phone layout is itself an open decision.
